items.title: Marsh Raises Treasury Allocation to Neutral on Elevated Yields
items.description: US investment consultancy Marsh is raising its Treasury allocation in some portfolios recommended to clients, a sign that large investors aim to take advantage of elevated yields.

items.title: Gabon Bonds Surge After Government Audit Finds Lower Debt Stock
items.description: Gabon’s bonds surged after the government announced that an audit found the OPEC member’s debt stock stood at $16.7 billion, almost a fifth below an initial estimate.

items.title: Russia’s Nornickel Seeks New Partner to Process Copper in China
items.description: Russia’s MMC Norilsk Nickel PJSC is talking with a new Chinese partner about a copper processing deal that would enable it to shut down a heavily polluting plant in the Arctic city of Norilsk.

items.title: Singapore’s Air Quality Reaches Worst Since 2019
items.description:
Singapore is shrouded in haze, with smoke from wildfires in neighboring Indonesia raising islandwide pollution to levels that pose a health risk.

Gabrielle Ng has more.  (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: S&P Warns of Credit, Earnings Risks at Indonesian State Lenders
items.description: Indonesia’s state-owned banks face rising credit and earnings risks after government-driven lending pushed loan growth to more than twice the industry pace, according to S&P Global Ratings.

items.description: The 10-year US Treasury yield rose to the highest in almost two decades, the latest milestone in a bruising global bond selloff driven by surging energy prices, mounting debt and inflation.

items.description: Gold held a decline as increasing disruptions to oil flows from the Middle East reinforced expectations the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates as soon as this week.

items.description: US stocks fell as elevated oil prices fueled further selling in Treasuries, pushing the 10-year yield to levels last seen 19 years ago and keeping risk appetite firmly in check.

items.title: Puig Agrees to Take Control of Isdin in €1.2 Billion Deal
items.description: Puig Brands SA agreed to buy the 50% of Isdin SA it didn’t already own for €1.2 billion ($1.4 billion), giving it full control of the skincare brand. Shares fell.
